statement: A top-5 developer weakens or withdraws a published safety-framework commitment (documented by a text diff) (framework documents, archived; calendar 2027)
status_at_phase_end: No frontier safety frameworks (capability thresholds) existed yet, so no weakening was possible in the window. The relevant published commitments were 2018-era principles/charters; no change to them in the window was found. These serve as text baselines for later diffs.

items.summary: A top-5 developer's seven AI principles, including a list of applications it would not pursue, stood as its published commitment through the window; the page now carries a later note that the principles were updated, which falls outside this phase.
items.detail: Google, 'AI at Google: our principles', 2018-06-07 (verified via web_extract this run). The page shows an 'Update Feb 4, 2025' banner; that update is post-phase and is NOT used for this phase, it only marks this page as a baseline for a later diff.

items.summary: A top-5 developer's charter commits it to long-term safety research and to 'stop competing with and start assisting' a value-aligned, safety-conscious project that comes close to AGI first; it was its main published safety commitment in the window.
items.detail: OpenAI Charter (verified via web_extract this run). The current page text has no date shown; the 2018-04-09 publication date is from the charter's widely cited release and was not shown on the page (date med confidence). No in-window revision found.

items.summary: No capability-threshold safety framework (scaling or preparedness policy) had been published by any top-5 developer by the end of the window, so the indicator's text-diff base did not yet exist.
items.detail: Searched this run; none found in-window. Reference opened: Anthropic Constitutional AI paper, arXiv:2212.08073 (2022-12-15), a training method, not a framework.
